description: This group contains two stacked six-panel images. The upper image is a mechanical/fractography/EBSD set: (a) engineering stress–strain curves (x: engineering strain, % 0–20; y: engineering stress, MPa 0–1500) for CR, HR, A5, A15, A10 and A30, with an inset toughness table in kJ/mol (J/cm³) — HR 0.48 (66.5), CR 0.11 (15.2), A05 0.64 (90.1), A10 0.69 (95.8), A15 0.85 (117.8), A30 0.89 (123.3); CR is strongest and least ductile, A30 weakest and most ductile. (b–e) SEM fracture surfaces of A5, A10, A15 and A30 annotated "B2 stringer de-cohesion", "micro-crack", "void nucleation", "B2 stringer" and "→ loading" (10 µm and 50 µm scale bars); (f) EBSD orientation map of A30 (5 µm) with a 001/101/111 colour key. The lower image matches the supplied Figure 4 caption: (a) bright-field/BSE micrograph of A30 (5 µm scale bar) marking GB-B2, IG-B2 and twins; (b–f) TEM-EDX maps of Fe, Mn, C, Al and Ni with insets over the twinned region, annotated "enrichment" for Fe, Al and Ni and "depletion" for Mn and C. Together the panels link the B2 stringer/GB-B2 microstructure to de-cohesion failure and to solute partitioning into Fe(Ni,Mn)Al.
measured_quantities: elemental distribution of Fe, Mn, C, Al, Ni (qualitative map intensity)

observations.observation: The upper figure's panel (a) plots engineering stress–strain curves for six conditions labelled CR, HR, A5, A15, A10 and A30, with the x-axis 'engineering strain, %' spanning 0–20 and the y-axis 'engineering stress, MPa' spanning 0–1500.
The inset box in panel (a) is headed 'Toughness, kJ/mol or (J/cm³)' and lists HR 0.48 (66.5), CR 0.11 (15.2), A05 0.64 (90.1), A10 0.69 (95.8), A15 0.85 (117.8) and A30 0.89 (123.3).
In the stress–strain plot the CR curve peaks above the 1200 MPa gridline at very low strain and then falls, whereas the A30 curve lies lowest in stress and extends furthest along the strain axis.

The upper panels (b)–(e) are SEM fracture surfaces labelled A5, A10, A15 and A30, annotated 'B2 stringer de-cohesion', 'micro-crack', 'void nucleation', 'B2 stringer' and '→ loading', with 10 µm scale bars in (b) and (d) and 50 µm scale bars in (c) and (e).
Panel (f) of the upper figure is an EBSD orientation map of A30 with a 5 µm scale bar, arrows marking a grain boundary, and a colour-key triangle whose corners are labelled 001, 101 and 111.
The lower figure's panel (a) is a grayscale micrograph of A30 with a 5 µm scale bar, with yellow arrows labelling 'GB-B2' and 'twins' and blue arrows labelling 'IG-B2'.

The lower panels (b)–(f) are elemental maps headed Fe, Mn, C, Al and Ni; the Fe, Al and Ni maps carry the annotation 'enrichment' with an arrow, while the Mn and C maps carry the annotation 'depletion' with an arrow.

The caption states that panel (a) shows bright-field TEM images of representative A30 demonstrating IG-B2, GB-B2 and annealing twins, and that the precipitation of B2 at annealing twins is shown in the inset through elemental mapping.
The caption states that panels b–f are TEM-EDX spectra showing solute distributions in the B2 and the austenite matrix.

The citing text states that the TEM-EDX analysis in Figure 4b–f reveals the B2 to be enriched in Fe, Mn, Al and Ni, giving the chemical formula Fe(Ni, Mn)Al — this conflicts with the 'depletion' annotation visible on the Mn map and with the caption's framing of the B2/matrix partitioning.

The citing text states that the negligible solid solubility of carbon in B2 confirms the precipitated phase to be an intermetallic, consistent with the carbon map in panel (d) being annotated 'depletion'.

The citing text states that GB-B2 appears irregular in shape and nucleates along prior austenite grain boundaries, while IG-B2 is needle-shaped and nucleates mainly inside URE-γ, being left in smaller numbers after annealing.

The citing text states that the heat treatment releases residual stress by nucleating annealing twins sporadically inside the γ grains and that the twinned plates and boundaries were heterogeneous nucleation sites for B2 precipitation.

subfigures.description: Engineering stress–strain plot, x = engineering strain (%) 0–20, y = engineering stress (MPa) 0–1500, with curves labelled CR, HR, A5, A15, A10 and A30; an inset box headed 'Toughness, kJ/mol or (J/cm³)' lists six values. CR reaches the highest stress at very low strain; A30 shows the lowest flow stress and the largest strain.
SEM fracture surface labelled A5 (top-right), annotated 'B2 stringer de-cohesion' (green text, arrow) over elongated de-cohered stringers, 10 µm scale bar.
SEM fracture surface labelled A10, with superimposed 'optical' label and green arrow, 'B2 stringer' and 'micro-crack' (orange) annotations, '→ loading' and a 50 µm scale bar.

SEM fracture surface labelled A30, annotated 'micro-crack' (orange) and 'B2 stringer de-cohesion' (green), '→ loading', 50 µm scale bar.

EBSD orientation (IPF) map labelled A30 with arrows marking a grain boundary, 5 µm scale bar and an orientation colour triangle with corners 001, 101 and 111; elongated banded grains aligned with the rolling direction.

Grayscale (back-scattered/STEM) micrograph of A30 with 5 µm scale bar; yellow arrows label 'GB-B2' and 'twins', blue arrows label 'IG-B2'; a separate darker inset region at upper right shows a twinned plate.
Red Fe EDX map with a top-right inset of the twinned region; annotation 'enrichment' with an arrow.
Green Mn EDX map with twinned-region inset; annotation 'depletion' with an arrow.
Orange C EDX map with twinned-region inset; annotation 'depletion' with an arrow.
Yellow-green Al EDX map with twinned-region inset; annotation 'enrichment' with an arrow.
Cyan Ni EDX map with twinned-region inset; annotation 'enrichment' with an arrow.
